correctness.rationale: A subset that becomes a singleton stays a singleton, so collapsing all singleton states to one absorbing reset state preserves shortest reset lengths in each factor and in the triple. Independently of the frozen signature quotient, I partitioned all 729 tables into 129 orbits under simultaneous state relabeling of both letters, found 94 synchronizing orbits of total mass 549 by subset reachability, and ran full product BFS over every multiset of three such orbit representatives. Weighting by the product of orbit sizes and 3! divided by the factorials of the orbit-index repetitions restores all ordered labeled triples. The exact length counts for 1–7 were 1062153, 48991068, 66420432, 35524872, 10653120, 2651616, and 165888, totaling 165469149. A separate word scan confirmed the 28 signatures and the six length-seven reset words for the specified witness, including 0010110; BFS excludes shorter words. The supplied seven-level signature quotient is also valid: each individually resettable subset graph has a singleton path of length at most six, right extensions preserve reset, and every signature triple had a nonempty intersection by seven. In arXiv v1 the cited product results are Lemma 5 and Proposition 7, not Lemma 3.1 and Proposition 3.4; this bibliographic slip does not enter the finite proof.
residual_risks: The exhaustive proof is for exactly three three-state complete synchronizing machines on the same ordered binary alphabet, with repeats and independent state labels; no extrapolation to other domains.
